protocol_type: Frame-based serial messaging protocol with optional flexible data-rate extension; content-addressed by IDENTIFIER; no opcode/command set at the wire layer; controller register-level command set via M_CAN's 512-byte register map.

channels.name: CAN bus
channels.description: Single shared channel carrying NRZ-coded bits; dominant overrides recessive; physical realization via ISO 11898-2 high-speed differential pair (external transceiver).

channels.name: Generic Slave Interface (Host CPU)
channels.description: 8/16/32-bit register access bus; allows Host to program registers + access Message RAM indirectly via the M_CAN's slave interface.

channels.name: Generic Master Interface (Message RAM)
channels.description: 32-bit external Message RAM access (single- or dual-ported); max 16K × 32-bit, one M_CAN uses ≤ 4.25K × 32-bit. Watched by RAM Watchdog (RWD).

frame_types.name: Classical CAN DATA FRAME
frame_types.purpose: 0..8-byte payload carried with 15-bit CRC; FDF = dominant; selected by Tx Buffer FDF = 0 or CCCR.FDOE = 0.

frame_types.name: Classical CAN REMOTE FRAME
frame_types.purpose: Request frame for matching IDENTIFIER; RTR = recessive; no DATA FIELD; only available in Classical CAN format. Tx Buffer T0.RTR = 1 transmits remote frame even when CCCR.FDOE = 1.

frame_types.name: CAN FD DATA FRAME
frame_types.purpose: 0..64-byte payload with 17-bit (≤16 B) or 21-bit (>16 B) CRC; FDF = recessive; selected by Tx Buffer FDF = 1; CCCR.FDOE must be 1.

frame_types.name: CAN FD DATA FRAME with Bit Rate Switching
frame_types.purpose: Like CAN FD DATA FRAME but BRS = 1 in Tx Buffer + CCCR.BRSE = 1; data phase from BRS to CRC delimiter transmitted at DBTP rate.

frame_types.name: ERROR FRAME
frame_types.purpose: Signals error; ACTIVE ERROR FLAG (6 dominant bits) for error-active node, PASSIVE ERROR FLAG (6 recessive bits) for error-passive node; both followed by ERROR DELIMITER (8 recessive bits).

frame_types.name: OVERLOAD FRAME
frame_types.purpose: Delays the next DATA / REMOTE FRAME; OVERLOAD FLAG (6 dominant bits) + OVERLOAD DELIMITER (8 recessive bits); max 2 consecutive per intermission.

data_frame_fields_classical.components: 11-bit standard ID + RTR  OR  11-bit ID + SRR + IDE + 18-bit extended ID + RTR (29-bit)

data_frame_fields_can_fd.components: 11-bit standard ID + RRS (always dominant)  OR  11-bit ID + SRR + IDE + 18-bit extended ID + RRS
r1 + FDF (recessive) + res (dominant) + BRS + ESI + DLC[3:0]
17-bit CRC (payload ≤16 B) OR 21-bit CRC (payload >16 B) + recessive CRC DELIMITER

control_field_bits_can_fd.rule: Receivers must accept any combination for forward compatibility.

control_field_bits_can_fd.purpose: Identifies frame format. Receiving FDF=1 with res=1 triggers Protocol Exception.
Bit Rate Switch — recessive enables data-phase bit-rate switch (DBTP) after BRS; only evaluated when CCCR.BRSE = 1 + CCCR.FDOE = 1.
Error State Indicator — dominant = transmitter error-active; recessive = transmitter error-passive.

data_length_code_encoding_classical.note: Classical CAN: DLC values 9..15 are coded the same as 8 (frame still carries 8 data bytes).

data_length_code_encoding_can_fd.note: CAN FD extends DLC encoding: codes 9..15 select 12/16/20/24/32/48/64 bytes per Table 54.

remote_frame_rules: Classical CAN only — there are NO REMOTE FRAMES in CAN FD format.
RTR bit = recessive (vs dominant for DATA FRAME) — classical.
Same IDENTIFIER as the requested DATA FRAME.
If a DATA FRAME and REMOTE FRAME with same IDENTIFIER start simultaneously, the DATA FRAME prevails (RTR dominant wins).
When Tx Buffer T0.RTR = 1, M_CAN transmits a remote frame per ISO 11898-1:2015 even if CCCR.FDOE = 1.
GFC.RRFS / RRFE reject all remote frames with standard / extended IDs respectively.
valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no AMBA-style per-cycle VALID/READY handshake on the CAN bus.
Frame-level ACK on bit 1 of ACK FIELD: receivers superscribe transmitter's recessive with dominant if CRC matched. In CAN FD frames the ACK delimiter accounts for the transmitter delay.
Bitwise arbitration on the ARBITRATION FIELD: each transmitter compares its driven bit to the monitored bus value; if drove recessive but bus is dominant, it loses arbitration and withdraws.
Generic Slave Interface (Host CPU side) is a register-mapped bus — no AMBA-VALID/READY but Protected-Write semantics on configuration registers (CCCR.CCE + CCCR.INIT = 1 required).
byte_order_within_data_field: MSB-first per byte; bytes within Tx/Rx Buffer Element packed 4 per 32-bit word (DB0 at bits 7:0, DB1 at bits 15:8, DB2 at bits 23:16, DB3 at bits 31:24 of T2/R2).

interframe_space.bus_idle: arbitrary length; any unit may start a transmission
interframe_space.suspend_transmission: 8 recessive bits added by an error-passive transmitter after its message
interframe_space.transmit_pause: 2 CAN bit times added by M_CAN after each successful transmission when CCCR.TXP = 1 (prevents babbling idiot scenarios).

tx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXBAR_AR_n: Host writes 1 to bit n of TXBAR to add Tx request for Buffer n; TXBRP.TRP_n is set when scan picks the request up.
tx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXBCR_CR_n: Host writes 1 to bit n of TXBCR to cancel transmission for Buffer n; TXBCF.CF_n is set on cancellation finish.
tx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXBTO_TO_n: Read-only status: Buffer n's transmission occurred successfully.
tx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXBCF_CF_n: Read-only status: Buffer n's transmission cancellation finished.
tx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXBTIE_TIE_n / TXBCIE_CFIE_n: Per-buffer interrupt enables for Tx complete / Tx cancellation finished.
tx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXFQS: Read-only Tx FIFO / Queue fill level + put / get indices.

rx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.RXF0A_F0AI / RXF1A_F1AI: Host writes the index of the last Rx FIFO element it has read into the FIFO Acknowledge register; M_CAN updates FnGI to F0AI+1, updates FnFL; host must write valid index (M_CAN does not validate).
rx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.NDAT1[n], NDAT2[n]: New Data flag per Rx Buffer n; set by M_CAN on Rx Buffer update; cleared by Host writing 1 to the bit position.
rx_handler_command_protocol_to_host.TXEFA_EFAI: Host writes the index of the last Tx Event FIFO element read; M_CAN updates EFGI to EFAI+1 + EFFL.

interrupt_command_protocol.IR_ack: Host writes 1 to corresponding IR bit to clear the flag (W1C); writing 0 has no effect.
interrupt_command_protocol.IE_route: IE register bit n = 1 enables interrupt source n on the selected interrupt line.
interrupt_command_protocol.ILS_route: ILS register bit n = 0 routes IR.n to m_can_int0; bit n = 1 routes to m_can_int1.
interrupt_command_protocol.ILE_enable: ILE.EINT0 / ILE.EINT1 enable / disable the two CPU interrupt lines independently.

test_mode_command_protocol.enter_test: Set CCCR.TEST = 1 while CCCR.INIT + CCCR.CCE = 1; gives write access to TEST register.
test_mode_command_protocol.loop_back_external: TEST.LBCK = 1 + CCCR.MON = 0; messages on m_can_tx are looped back to Rx internally; ACK errors ignored.
test_mode_command_protocol.loop_back_internal: TEST.LBCK = 1 + CCCR.MON = 1; m_can_rx disconnected, m_can_tx held recessive; "hot self-test" without bus disturbance.
test_mode_command_protocol.tx_pin_control: TEST.TX[1:0] = 00 (default normal), 01 (Sample Point at m_can_tx for monitoring), 10 (constant dominant), 11 (constant recessive).
test_mode_command_protocol.rx_pin_monitor: Read TEST.RX to monitor m_can_rx (0 = dominant, 1 = recessive).
